thread:
maya: Heads-up — seeing recurring p99 spikes on the 2:30-3:00PM window. Investigating, looks tied to kernel handshake stalls when KV hit rate drops.
jonathan: Can you paste the numbers? p95/p99 and what you mean by handshake stalls.
maya: p95 ~ 18ms, p99 jumping to 120-180ms on short seq workloads (seq_len <= 64). Perf trace shows extra 8–15ms spent in kernel selection + cuda graph capture on first few microbatches. KV cache miss bursts correlate.
kevin: perf-bot run summary: avg_batch_tokens 320, microbatch_count 3, kv_hit_rate 0.62, observed extra_launch_ms 12.
perf-bot: [automated] tail-heatmap run 2026-03-15 14:52 - p99=162ms, p95=19ms, mean=24ms, sample=10k reqs.
lina: Is this the kernel fallback path? We saw another case where falling back to the slow FP32 init path cost ~10ms per microbatch.
maya: Yep — looks like fallback from `fast_small_kern` -> `compat_kern` when microbatch shape differs and cache isn't warmed. Also cuda-graph capture triggers on first instance of a new shaped microbatch.
jonathan: So hypothesis: when max_batch_tokens is large we aggregate longer and produce fewer but bigger kernel shapes, but if KV misses cause re-slicing, we touch fallback. What are current scheduler params?
kevin: Current: `max_batch_tokens=4096`, `max_wait_ms=8`, `max_microbatch_size=128`.
maya: Proposed quick experiment: lower `max_batch_tokens` to 2048 and `max_wait_ms` to 4ms, enable `prefer_small_kernel=true` heuristic and add a fast-path gate when kv_hit_rate < 0.7 to force small-kernel dispatch. Expect fewer heavy captures and lower tail.
lina: I'd also try enabling `kv-prefetch=on` for short sequences to reduce miss bursts — might reduce the number of cold-kernel events.
jonathan: Can we get a baseline A/B? Run 30m with current config, then 30m with proposed. Need p50/p95/p99 + kernel-launch breakdown.
kevin: Running baseline now. Command I used: ```./perf-run --trace=kernel-handshake --duration=30m --bucket=short-seq``` will push to our perf dashboard.
maya: I ran a quick synthetic sim earlier: baseline p99=162ms, experiment (2048/4ms + prefer_small_kernel) p99=88ms, p95 stayed ~20ms, throughput dropped ~6%. Tail reduced significantly.
jonathan: 6% throughput loss for ~45% tail reduction might be acceptable for latency-sensitive routes. Which routes do we apply it to? All hosted API or just low-latency tokens?
lina: Target: chat short-turns (<=64 tokens) and realtime routes. Non-critical bulk embedding/long-gen traffic keep default.
kevin: Note: we saw one regression in QA when `prefer_small_kernel` forced an older kernel that has slightly worse quality for a specific multi-lingual model. We'll gate by model tag: `model.tags` not contain `rlhf-sensitive`.
maya: Also add metric: kernel_handshake_ms per-request and kv_hit_rate; alert if handshake_ms > 20ms for p99.
jonathan: Sounds good. Steps: 1) kevin run baseline, 2) maya deploy staged scheduler config to canary 10%, 3) run perf traces and compare, 4) rollback if any regressions in quality or error rate.
kevin: Starting baseline trace now. ETA 35m. I'll post raw csv when done. :gear:
maya: If we see any spike in model errors after forcing kernel variant, bail early. Also check GPU occupancy — small kernels might increase per-token latency if we over-shard.
lina: For the experiment, add a short TTL for kernel-graph captures so we don't hold captured graphs for >5min for weird shapes. That reduces memory churn.
jonathan: One more ask — can perf-bot annotate traces with `max_batch_tokens` and `max_wait_ms` at run time so we have metadata attached?
perf-bot: [automated] will attach scheduler config to the next run.
maya: OK. After kevin posts baseline CSV, I'll schedule the 10% canary and tag the experiment in the perf dashboard.
kevin: baseline done. Uploading CSV: https://internal.perf/trace/1715089400.csv
maya: Uploaded quick diff: p99 down from 162 -> 84, p95 stable, tokens/sec -6%. I'll paste histogram in the perf dashboard.
jonathan: Great. Let's move to 10% canary tomorrow at 09:00 PT. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
kevin: noted. Will also try a variant: keep `max_batch_tokens=4096` but set `max_microbatch_size=64` to see if smaller microbatches reduce shape diversity without hurting throughput. I'll include that in the canary matrix.
maya: Perfect. Closing loop after canary. If successful we update default scheduler policy and add model gating.
kevin: leaving logs in `/var/log/redwood/perf/1715088888-handshake-run.log` if anyone wants to debug.
lina: Tagging infra: @jonathan if we need quick rollback hooks.
jonathan: I have rollback playbook ready.
maya: Thanks — will follow up with a small runbook note in the eng-runtime docs.
